sections.heading: Section 1: Vector Arithmetic and Linear Combinations

questions.q: Is the vector $\mathbf{w} = [7, 4]$ a linear combination of $\mathbf{v}_1 = [1, 2]$ and $\mathbf{v}_2 = [3, -1]$?
choices: No, the vectors are linearly dependent
No, because the determinant is zero
questions.answer: Solve $c_1[1, 2] + c_2[3, -1] = [7, 4] \Rightarrow c_1 + 3c_2 = 7$ and $2c_1 - c_2 = 4 \Rightarrow c_2 = 2c_1 - 4$. Substitute: $c_1 + 6c_1 - 12 = 7 \Rightarrow 7c_1 = 19 \Rightarrow c_1 = 19/7, c_2 = 10/7$.

questions.q: What is the definition of the span of a set of vectors $\{\mathbf{v}_1, \dots, \mathbf{v}_k\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$?
choices: The set of all possible linear combinations $c_1\mathbf{v}_1 + \dots + c_k\mathbf{v}_k$ where $c_i \in \mathbb{R}$
The set of all vectors perpendicular to $\mathbf{v}_1$
The sum of the lengths of the vectors
The matrix formed by using the vectors as columns
questions.answer: By definition, $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}_1, \dots, \mathbf{v}_k\}$ is the subspace consisting of all linear combinations of those vectors.

questions.q: A set of vectors $\{\mathbf{v}_1, \dots, \mathbf{v}_k\}$ is linearly independent if and only if:
choices: At least one vector is a multiple of another
The dot product of any two vectors is zero
The number of vectors $k$ is greater than the dimension $n$
questions.answer: Linear independence requires that the only linear combination yielding the zero vector is the trivial solution where all coefficients are zero.

questions.q: Can any set of $4$ vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$ be linearly independent?
choices: No, any set of more than $n$ vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is guaranteed to be linearly dependent
Yes, provided none of the vectors is the zero vector
Yes, if they all have unit length
Only if their cross products are non-zero
questions.answer: By the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra, any collection of $k > n$ vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ must be linearly dependent because there are at most $n$ pivot columns.

questions.q: Are the vectors $\mathbf{v}_1 = [1, 2, 0]$, $\mathbf{v}_2 = [0, 1, 3]$, and $\mathbf{v}_3 = [2, 5, 3]$ linearly independent?
choices: No, because they contain a zero entry
questions.answer: Check: $2\mathbf{v}_1 + \mathbf{v}_2 = 2[1, 2, 0] + [0, 1, 3] = [2, 4+1, 3] = [2, 5, 3] = \mathbf{v}_3$. Since one vector is a combination of the others, the set is dependent.

sections.heading: Section 3: Dot Product, Norm, and Orthogonality

questions.q: Compute the Euclidean norm (length) of the vector $\mathbf{v} = [2, -3, 6]$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
Find the unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf{u} = [-1, 2, 2]$.
What does the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality state for any vectors $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^n$?
questions.answer: The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality states $|\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}| \leq \|\mathbf{u}\| \|\mathbf{v}\|$, with equality holding if and only if the vectors are collinear.

questions.q: What is the formula for the orthogonal projection of vector $\mathbf{y}$ onto a non-zero vector $\mathbf{u}$?
questions.answer: The projection of $\mathbf{y}$ onto the line spanned by $\mathbf{u}$ is $\frac{\mathbf{y} \cdot \mathbf{u}}{\|\mathbf{u}\|^2} \mathbf{u} = \frac{\mathbf{y} \cdot \mathbf{u}}{\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{u}} \mathbf{u}$.

questions.q: If $\hat{\mathbf{y}} = \text{proj}_{\mathbf{u}}(\mathbf{y})$, what is the geometric relationship between $\mathbf{z} = \mathbf{y} - \hat{\mathbf{y}}$ and $\mathbf{u}$?
questions.answer: By the Orthogonal Decomposition Theorem, any vector can be uniquely decomposed into a component parallel to $\mathbf{u}$ and an orthogonal component $\mathbf{z} \perp \mathbf{u}$.
